terms.name: Chaperoning
terms.definition: The continuing supervisory activity of independently observing consequential behavior, exercising informed judgment, and intervening effectively when appropriate. This requires access, competence, authority, and an actual ability to alter outcomes—not nominal participation or an agent merely stating that an action is inappropriate.

terms.name: Horizon compression
terms.definition: A process in which the time available to identify, interpret, decide about, and intervene in consequential activity becomes shorter relative to the time intervention requires. It is an intervention-window problem, not a general label for every obstacle to correcting an agent.

terms.name: Sleight-of-hand effect
terms.definition: An analogy for a mismatch between apparently successful local observation and the consequential process actually unfolding. An observer may see what was assigned for monitoring while missing actions or relationships elsewhere that change the outcome. Deliberate concealment is not required.
